bio:
In 2019, Paramount Pictures released the first trailer for the live-action Sonic the Hedgehog movie. To the horror of fans worldwide, the initial design attempted to make Sonic look visually grounded in reality. The resulting character featured tiny, separated eyes, thin lanky limbs, human-like hands, and a mouth full of creepy, hyper-realistic human teeth.

The internet instantly revolted, flooding social media with backlash and memes. The criticism was so severe that the movie was delayed so the studio could entirely redesign Sonic to match his classic gaming look. The original model was shelved, and the internet affectionately dubbed the discarded design "Ugly Sonic."

Nowadays, Ugly Sonic is treated as a real-life actor living in a world shared by humans and cartoons. He was cast as the lead role in the 2020 movie but was abruptly fired after the initial trailer caused widespread internet mockery. Unphased by his "haters on the internet," Ugly Sonic works the fan convention circuit, signing autographs and boasting that he has a big new reality travel show coming out. He ultimately transitions from a laughingstock to a genuine hero, leveraging his connections to team up with the FBI to bust a cartoon counterfeiting ring.
